name: OGLE-LMC-ECL-09114 A
description: The primary star of the eclipsing binary OGLE-LMC-ECL-09114, 3.304 solar masses and 26.33 solar radii; the two stars eclipse each other every 214.366 days.

radius.source: Primary radius (solar radii) 26.33 +/- 0.34, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Graczyk et al. (2018ApJ...860....1G)

mass.source: Primary mass (solar masses) 3.304 +/- 0.023, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Graczyk et al. (2018ApJ...860....1G)

temperature.source: Primary log Teff 3.719 +/- 0.005, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Graczyk et al. (2018ApJ...860....1G): 5236 K

gravity.source: Primary log g 2.116 +/- 0.011, as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) lists it from Graczyk et al. (2018ApJ...860....1G)

distance.source: Pietrzynski et al. (2019), Nature 567, 200, Table 1: distance modulus 18.490 +/- 0.028 for OGLE-LMC-ECL-09114, converted here as 10^(1 + m/5) pc

text.card: The primary star of OGLE-LMC-ECL-09114, a pair that eclipse each other every 214.366 days.
text.introduction: It has 3.304 solar masses and 26.33 solar radii; its partner has 3.205 and 18.79, measured from the eclipses and the stars' motions.
text.locator: DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164), OGLE-LMC-ECL-09114: Mass, Radius and Period, from Graczyk et al. (2018ApJ...860....1G)

notes: Masses, radii and temperatures as DEBCat (Southworth 2015, ASPC 496, 164) (https://www.astro.keele.ac.uk/jkt/debcat/) lists them from Graczyk et al. (2018ApJ...860....1G); Pietrzynski et al. (2013Natur.495...76P).
SIMBAD knows the system as OGLE LMC-ECL-09114 but links no Gaia DR3 source; it is placed at the Gaia DR3 source 0.47 arcsec from SIMBAD's position, G = 16.46 against DEBCat's V = 16.71.

radialVelocity.source: No catalogued radial velocity: Gaia DR3 measures none for source 4658260373306002944 and SIMBAD lists none. Zero is assumed; a 30 km/s error moves the star by one part in 20,000,000 of its distance per century
